pairs.question: Cur igitur incendium curiae, oppugnationem aedium M. Lepidi, caedem hanc ipsam contra rem publicam senatus factam esse decrevit?
pairs.answer: Quia nulla vis umquam est in libera civitate suscepta inter civis non contra rem publicam.
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses a genuine 'Cur...?' interrogative and immediately answers it himself with 'quia...'. Question taken whole through the '?'; answer is the contiguous 'quia' clause to its full stop (stops before 'Non enim est illa defensio...', which begins a new point). Section marker '13.' and surrounding scaffolding excluded; first word of answer capitalized for presentation.

pairs.question: Tulit enim de caede quae in Appia via facta esset, in qua P. Clodius occisus esset. Quid ergo tulit?
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question 'Quid ergo tulit?'; the preceding verbatim sentence is kept as setup (rule 2) so the subject (Pompeius) and 'tulit' have a referent. Answer is the immediate self-reply through its full stop; stops before the next volley 'Quid porro quaerendum est?' Section marker '15.' / 'At enim Cn. Pompeius...' framing excluded; answer's first word capitalized.

pairs.question: Num igitur ulla quaestio de Africani morte lata est?
pairs.derivation: Genuine 'Num...?' interrogative answered by Cicero himself. 'de Africani morte' makes the question self-contained. Answer is the immediate self-reply 'certe nulla' through its full stop; stops before the following 'Quid ita? quia...' (a separate, weaker self-contained micro-pair dropped to avoid overlap, preferring false negatives). Section markers and first-word capitalization normalized.
